_about: Ruin tags: the one situation a dungeon is now in, which supplies its enemies, its leader (the boss in the climax room), an ally or witness inside, a complication, a signature reward, the places it has made of the rooms and what can be seen of it - the cohesion engine of Kevin Crawford's Worlds Without Number ruins (one tag giving linked enemies, friends, complications, things and places; read through secondary sources only, the book itself not reachable). Read by rules/dungeons.py; authored game data, world-agnostic, and no model writes any of it. `enemies` and `leader` name codex people by their exact base (`people`, rules/npcs.py) or bestiary creatures by exact id (`creatures`), priced through the encounter budget at the party's APL; never a humanoid race, which is the world's own (the-world-owns-its-own-races). `hostile` false means people who are wary of strangers and do not attack on sight. `ally.people` is a codex base; the ally is a real actor, met in the dungeon's second room (the Five Room Dungeon's role-play room, B/X's 'special' room). `places` are by family (built, natural, dug), in order inward, the last being the leader's lair and the climax. `traces` are what the situation has left that can be seen, one per room, shown and never explained; `revelation` is the last room's, the thing that ties the story together. `rumour` is what {town} says, joined to the local attitude; `quest` is the quest's title. Slots: {leader} {lair} {ally} {town} {where} {age}.

smugglers-war.situation: two crews of smugglers are fighting over the run, and one crew holds it

ally.notes: A lookout of the rival crew, caught and tied up here two days ago; says {leader} keeps the crew's takings in {lair} and sleeps with the key on a cord round the neck.

smugglers-war.complication: The rival crew means to come down soon, and will take anyone they find below for one of the enemy.

reward.said: the crew's takings, in coin of a dozen mints

built: lamps by the dozen, trimmed and filled and ready
hammocks slung between the pillars, and kit stowed under them
a room curtained off with sailcloth, a real bed in it
natural: nets hung across the cave to dry
a ring of stones, fresh ash and a blackened kettle
a dry hollow in the rock, a cot in it, a sailcloth curtain

traces: Fresh crates are stacked over the old ones, stencilled with the marks of no house in {town}.
Blood on the floor has been scrubbed at and not scrubbed out, and a knife is left stuck in a beam.
smugglers-war.revelation: The master's papers name the rival crew's captain, and both crews sell to the same buyer in {town}: whoever pays them wants them at each other's throats.
smugglers-war.rumour: lamps have been seen moving in {where} at night, where no lamp should be
smugglers-war.quest: Find who works the old run below {where}

bandit-hideout.situation: a band of road-robbers hides below, with a prisoner held for ransom

ally.notes: Taken on the road for ransom and kept here since; heard {leader} tell the band the ransom is never coming, and that they are to move on and leave nobody behind.

bandit-hideout.complication: The traveller's family in {town} have already paid the band once.

reward.said: the band's road-takings

built: a stool by a spy-hole, and a bell-rope
saddles, harness and boxes, heaped high
a table with a map on it and a good chair
natural: a ledge with a view back down the way in
a cave heaped with saddlebags and broken boxes
a dry cave with a hide on the floor and a lantern

traces: Stolen saddles and harness are heaped by the wall, some still marked with their owners' brands.
A map of the roads out of {town} is drawn on a hide, the lonely stretches ringed in charcoal.
bandit-hideout.revelation: The captain's tally splits the take six ways, and one of the six shares goes to somebody in {town}'s own watch.
bandit-hideout.rumour: travellers on the roads near {town} have gone missing, and some were last seen near {where}
bandit-hideout.quest: Find where the road-robbers hide below {where}

restless-dead.situation: the dead have risen, because the rites that kept them stopped

ally.notes: Came down to say the old rites for the dead and was cut off by them; says the dead began to walk when the rites stopped, and that the first of them lies in {lair}.

restless-dead.complication: Some of the dead wear the rings and buckles of families still living in {town}.

reward.said: grave-gold, laid in the coffin for the journey

built: graves dug out from below, the earth thrown upward
bones pulled down from the niches and heaped
a tomb older than the rest, its lid broken outward
natural: cairns of stones pulled apart from inside
a low cave carpeted with bones
a barrow chamber at the very end, its door-stone fallen

traces: Coffin lids lie pushed aside, and the nails are bent outward.
Bare footprints in the dust go round and round the room in a ring, and none lead out of it.
restless-dead.revelation: The oldest tomb's inscription asks the living to keep the rites or wake the dead; the last rite cut beside it was said {age}.
restless-dead.rumour: the old graves have been found open, and dogs will not go near
restless-dead.quest: Lay the dead to rest below {where}

spider-nest.situation: spiders have taken the place and spun it full

ally.notes: A trapper wrapped in silk and hung from the roof, still alive; says the spiders came up out of {lair}, and that the brood-mother has never once come out of it.

spider-nest.complication: Not all the cocooned shapes are dead, and cutting them down means working under the webs.

reward.said: a dead traveller's purse, wrapped up with him

built: grey silk hung in sheets from wall to wall
shapes wrapped in silk and hung in rows
a room heaped with egg sacs the size of loaves
natural: a cave closed off by a curtain of silk
wrapped shapes hung from the roof
a cave heaped with egg sacs
dug: a drift strung across with silk
an old stope hung with wrapped shapes
the last working, heaped with egg sacs

traces: Silk hangs in grey sheets, and things are wrapped in it, some the size of a man.
Husks of beetles and rats lie drained in drifts under the webs.
spider-nest.revelation: Under the eggs lie a half-burned torch and the bones of the trapper's lost companion: they came down a season ago to burn the nest out, and fed it instead.
spider-nest.rumour: dogs and goats go missing at the edge of {town}, and trappers will not set lines near {where} any more

ghoul-pack.situation: ghouls have made it their feeding ground, and drag the dead down from above

ally.notes: Came down after the bodies stolen from {town}'s burial ground and hid when he saw what took them; says they drag everything to {lair}.

ghoul-pack.complication: One of the ghouls was a gravedigger of {town}, and the man hiding here knew him.

reward.said: rings and buckles taken off the dead

built: bones split along their length lie everywhere
a passage worn smooth by what is dragged along it
a hall with a long stone table, and what is left on it
natural: split bones lie thick on the floor
a cave with a flat rock in the middle, stained dark

traces: Bones lie split along their length, the marrow gone, and the marks on them are of teeth.
Drag-marks run in from the way in, a great many of them, and none run out.
ghoul-pack.revelation: Among the bones in {lair} lie the pack-leader's own grave-goods, with its name on them: it was buried here once, and it was the first to wake hungry.
ghoul-pack.rumour: graves in {town}'s burial ground have been found dug up from below

cult-below.situation: a cult meets below in secret and is calling up something old

ally.notes: Taken from {town} three nights ago to be given at the next rite; says {leader} has promised the others something that answers from {lair}.

cult-below.complication: Some of the cult are people of {town}, with families who will want them home alive.

reward.said: the cult's offerings, coin its members gave

built: hooded robes on a row of pegs
a hall with a circle painted on the floor
a small room, black-walled, a stone in its middle
natural: robes hung on pegs driven into the rock
a circle painted on the cave floor
a still black pool at the end of the cave

traces: A dozen hooded robes hang on pegs, and the hems are wet.
A circle is painted on the floor in something dark, and the paint is new.
cult-below.revelation: The speaker's notes show the cult found the old signs already cut here and only painted over them: whatever answers in {lair} was answering long before them.
cult-below.rumour: people of {town} have been seen going down at night in their best clothes, and coming back with nothing to say

rat-king.situation: rats rule it, and a man who commands them

ally.notes: Ran down here from {town} to hide and got lost; says the rats do what a man tells them, and he lives in {lair}.

rat-king.complication: The man who commands the rats was a beggar of {town}, and the town let him starve.

reward.said: coins and buttons the rats carried in

built: every wooden thing gnawed to a stump
rags and straw heaped higher than a man
a seat built up out of the town's rubbish
natural: a cave crossed by runs worn smooth
a cave heaped with rags and straw
a seat built up out of rubbish at the back of the cave

traces: Every wooden thing has been gnawed down to a stump, door-frames and all.
The rats' runs are worn smooth along the walls, and they all lead the same way.
rat-king.revelation: The throne in {lair} is built of {town}'s refuse, and sewn into it are scraps with the names of everyone who ever turned the rat-king from their door.
rat-king.rumour: the rats in {town} have grown bold, and there are more of them every week
rat-king.quest: Find what drives the rats below {where}

ooze-in-the-works.situation: an ooze has grown in the damp and eats whatever comes down

ally.notes: A drain-worker of {town} who came down to clear a blockage and has been cornered on a ledge since; says the blockage moved, and went back to {lair}.

ooze-in-the-works.complication: The drain-worker's mate came down with him, and was the first thing it ate.

reward.said: coins, buckles and rings it could not eat

built: a channel whose walls shine wet
a room scoured to the bare stone
a deep square cistern, its surface very still
dug: a drift whose walls shine wet
props eaten through at the foot, the roof sagging
the sump at the bottom, its water very still

traces: The walls are scoured clean in a band at floor height, as if something wiped them as it passed.
Bones lie here so clean they shine, with no mark of a tooth on them.
ooze-in-the-works.revelation: In {lair} lies everything it could not eat, and among it the seal of {town}'s drain-masters: they knew it was down here, and stopped sending men to the bottom.
ooze-in-the-works.rumour: the drain-workers of {town} have stopped going below the third grating, and will not say why
ooze-in-the-works.quest: Clear what blocks the old works below {where}

beast-lair.situation: a great beast has denned below and hunts the land above

ally.notes: A hunter from {town} who tracked the beast here and fell; says it drags its kills to {lair} and sleeps through the middle of the day.

beast-lair.complication: The beast has young with it.

reward.said: what the hunters before carried, their purses still on them

natural: the floor trodden to dust, tufts of fur on the rock
gnawed bones of cattle in heaps
a warm hollow that stinks of beast
built: a hall whose floor is trodden to dust
bones of cattle heaped against the walls
a room bedded deep in torn straw and hide

traces: The floor is trodden to dust and scattered with tufts of fur.
Gnawed bones of cattle lie in heaps, and the heaps are older the further in.
beast-lair.revelation: Among the bones in {lair} is a collar from {town}'s kennels: it was somebody's beast once, and it got loose.
beast-lair.rumour: cattle have been taken off the hills above {town}, dragged away whole
beast-lair.quest: Hunt the beast that dens below {where}

weeping-ghost.situation: a ghost lives the night it died over and over, and will not let the place be
weeping-ghost.who: a ghost and what it has woken

leader.title: the one who will not leave

ally.notes: Came down to read the old inscriptions and stayed too long; says the ghost repeats one night over and over, the night the place fell, and is strongest in {lair}.

weeping-ghost.complication: The ghost was wronged, and whoever wronged it has descendants living in {town}.

reward.said: what the ghost died guarding

built: a hall where breath smokes, though the air is still
furniture shoved against the walls in a ring
a small room, a stain on the floor that never dried

traces: Furniture stands shoved against the walls in a ring, some of it stacked to the ceiling.
Words are scrawled in the dust of a table, the same three words written over and over.
weeping-ghost.revelation: In {lair} the ghost's own body lies where it fell, and the knife in its back bears the mark of a house still standing in {town}.
weeping-ghost.rumour: folk hear weeping from under the ground at night, always at the same hour

the-guardians.situation: the builders' guardians are still on duty, and nobody told them to stop

ally.notes: A treasure-seeker who got in and cannot get back out past the guardians; says they stand still until something crosses the threshold of {lair}.

the-guardians.complication: The guardians were set to keep something in, not to keep people out.

reward.said: what the guardians were set to keep

built: empty niches along the walls, each the shape of a man
a hall with marks on the floor where heavy feet have paced
a round room with one door and a great chest in it

traces: Niches line the walls, each the shape of a man, and some of them are empty.
Scratches on the floor show where heavy feet have paced the same line for years.
the-guardians.revelation: The guardians' orders are cut over the door of {lair}: keep it shut until the makers come back. The makers never came back, and the guardians never stopped.
the-guardians.rumour: something below has been heard walking, slow and heavy, and never stopping
the-guardians.quest: Get past what keeps watch below {where}

fungus-garden.situation: a fungus has taken it over and grows as if it were tended

ally.notes: Came down for the pale caps that grow nowhere else and breathed something in; says the growth thinks, and its heart is in {lair}.

fungus-garden.complication: The herbalist's cure grows only in the growth's own heart, so burning it out burns the cure too.

reward.said: a chest grown over, its coin gone green

natural: pale caps in rows too straight to be wild
a cave whose walls pulse faintly
built: pale caps growing in rows across the floor
a chamber whose walls pulse faintly
dug: pale caps in rows along the drift
an old stope thick with drifting spores
the last working, its walls pulsing faintly

traces: Pale caps grow in rows too straight to be wild, as if somebody once planted them.
A skeleton lies sprouting, the fungus grown through it where the flesh was.
fungus-garden.revelation: The rows were planted: whoever kept the place before farmed the caps, and when they left, the crop went on farming itself, out of {lair}.
fungus-garden.rumour: the people who went down for mushrooms came back speaking slowly, and then not at all
fungus-garden.quest: Find the heart of what grows below {where}

the-roost.situation: bats and blood-drinkers roost in it in their thousands

ally.notes: Digs guano for {town}'s tanners and was trapped by the swarm; says {leader} hangs in {lair}, and the swarm goes out at dusk.

the-roost.complication: The guano-diggers of {town} need the roost for their living.

reward.said: somebody's savings, buried under the guano

natural: guano a foot deep, and a stink like a wall
a roof alive with small hanging bodies
a cave so high the light does not reach its roof
built: a ceiling alive with small hanging bodies
a tall room, its ceiling lost in the dark

traces: Guano lies a foot deep and the stink is a wall.
The roof moves: thousands of small bodies, hanging and shifting.
the-roost.revelation: Under the great roost lie a buried sack and the bones of the digger who hid it, the one {town} said ran off with the guild's money.
the-roost.rumour: the bats come out thicker every dusk, and they have taken to biting

drowned-works.situation: it has flooded, and something big lives in the water
drowned-works.who: things that live in the water

ally.notes: Has been on a dry ledge since the water came up; says something big swims in {lair}, and the water is still rising.

reward.said: the pay of the last shift, never handed out

dug: water waist deep and black, the props rotting in it
a stope flooded to the chest
a black pool at the bottom, very deep
built: water to the knee over the floor
a room flooded to the chest
a room that is all water, very deep
natural: water to the knee, and cold
a cave flooded to the chest
a pool in the rock, very deep and black

traces: The water is black and cold, and things float in the eddies: a boot, a lamp, a hat.
A sluice wheel stands with its gate wedged open by an iron bar.
drowned-works.revelation: The flood was let in on purpose: the sluice to {lair} was opened from the inside, and the opener's name is chalked beside it.
drowned-works.rumour: the water in {town}'s wells has gone brackish, and the old men say it comes up from {where}
drowned-works.quest: Find what lives in the water below {where}

dead-miners.situation: the miners who never came up are still working

ally.notes: Came down looking for her husband's body; says the foreman drove them all deeper even after the roof began to talk, and he is still down in {lair}.

dead-miners.complication: The widow's husband is among the dead, and still working.

reward.said: the coin the dead men's ore was worth, never collected

dug: a drift with fresh spoil heaped along it
a stope where the picks still hang on their hooks
the deepest working, a tally chalked on the wall
natural: a cave where the picks still hang on their hooks
the deepest cut, a tally chalked on the wall

traces: Spoil is heaped fresh along the drift, and nobody living has been down to dig it.
The picks hang on their hooks, and their blades are bright from use.
dead-miners.revelation: The foreman's tally is chalked across the wall of {lair} and is still going: a count of loads for every day since the roof fell, in a hand that is not alive.
dead-miners.rumour: miners swear they hear picks working below the old mine at night
dead-miners.quest: Put the dead miners to rest below {where}

stone-wakes.situation: the diggers woke something that sleeps in the rock

ally.notes: Came after a vein of crystal and woke what sleeps in the rock; says it comes out of {lair} when the walls ring.

stone-wakes.complication: The crystal it guards is what {town}'s smiths would pay the most for.

reward.said: raw gems prised out of the walls

dug: a drift whose walls hum when touched
a stope split by long fresh cracks
a working that stops at a wall of crystal
natural: a cave whose walls hum when touched
a cave split by long fresh cracks
a hollow lined with crystal from floor to roof
built: a hall split by long fresh cracks
a room whose walls hum when touched
a vault burst open from inside the rock

traces: The walls are split in long fresh cracks, and the cracks hum faintly.
Rock bulges out of the wall in the shape of a reaching hand, and there are more of them further in.
stone-wakes.revelation: In {lair} the digging stops at a wall of crystal, and the stone is shaped like a face: the diggers cut into something that was asleep.
stone-wakes.rumour: the ground under {town} has been shaking, small shakes, every few nights
stone-wakes.quest: Learn what wakes in the rock below {where}

the-kept-beast.situation: the beast the last owners kept got loose and ate them

ally.notes: The last of the crew, hiding up with the cargo; says they kept the beast to frighten off the watch, it ate the crew instead, and now it lairs in {lair}.

the-kept-beast.complication: The smuggler wants the cargo, and will not leave without it.

reward.said: the coin the crew never got to spend

built: a pen of iron bars, the bars bent outward
bunks torn apart, nobody's things left whole
a pool where something heavy lies up in the warm
natural: a pen of iron bars across a cave, the bars bent outward
a camp torn apart, nothing left whole
a hollow that stinks of beast

traces: A pen of iron bars stands open, the bars bent outward from inside.
Bunks are torn apart and nobody's things are left whole.
the-kept-beast.revelation: The crew's last ledger, found in {lair}, shows they bought the beast from a dealer in {town} who still sells them.
the-kept-beast.rumour: a dog that went down a drain in {town} came up in pieces

deserters.situation: deserters from a war hide below and will hang anyone who betrays them

ally.notes: Ran with the others and wants only to go home; says {leader} will hang anyone who tries, and keeps the company's pay chest in {lair}.

deserters.complication: They deserted from a battle {town} still calls a victory.

reward.said: a season's wages for a whole company

built: a barricade of tables and a lookout's stool
a long table, tin plates, a cold stove
a camp bed, a field desk and a locked chest

traces: Uniforms are cut up for rags, the badges torn off and thrown in a heap.
A list of names is pinned up, some of them struck through, and the lines are fresh.
deserters.revelation: The sergeant's orders are still in his coat in {lair}: the company was sent to be lost, so that its lord could keep the pay.
deserters.rumour: soldiers who never came home from the last war are said to have been seen near {where}

the-taken.situation: people-takers keep the people they steal here, until they can be sold on

ally.notes: Taken from a workshop in {town} a week ago; says they are all to be shipped out, and {leader} keeps the list of the taken in {lair}.

the-taken.complication: The list of the taken names people {town} believes simply ran away.

reward.said: the price of the people already sold

built: pens of new timber along an old wall
a table, dice and a cudgel
a desk with a ledger on it and a good lamp
natural: pens of new timber across a cave
a ledge with a table, dice and a cudgel
a dry cave with a desk and a ledger

traces: Chains hang from new staples driven into old walls.
Bowls and a water butt stand by the pens, enough for a dozen.
the-taken.revelation: The dealer's list in {lair} names the buyers as well as the taken, and one of the buyers is a household of {town}.
the-taken.rumour: young people of {town} have gone missing, and the watch says they ran off

thieves-den.situation: a thieves' guild keeps its den and its counting-house below

ally.notes: A fence who owes the guild and was put down here to work it off; says {leader} counts the take in {lair} at midnight, alone.

thieves-den.complication: Half the stolen goods belong to people of {town} who cannot say how they lost them.

reward.said: the guild's share of a year's thieving

built: a room of shelves, every shelf full of somebody else's things
long tables heaped with purses and trinkets
a room with a heavy table and a set of scales

traces: Purses lie cut open and emptied in a heap by the door, dozens of them.
Locks of every kind are nailed to a board for practice, and every one of them is picked.
thieves-den.revelation: The keeper's book in {lair} shows the guild pays {town}'s magistrate a share each month, and has for years.
thieves-den.rumour: every thief taken in {town} lately has gone free by morning

crawling-stores.situation: vermin have bred in rotten stores that somebody hid instead of burning

ally.notes: A ratcatcher of {town} hired to clear the stores, who found worse than rats; says the biggest of them nests in {lair}, under the rotten grain.

crawling-stores.complication: The stores' owner in {town} sold the rotten grain on, and wants nobody to see where it was kept.

reward.said: coin hidden under the grain and never declared

built: split sacks of grain gone black
a heap of rotten grain taller than a man
dug: sacks of grain gone black, stacked in a drift
a drift whose floor moves underfoot
a working heaped with rotten grain

traces: Grain sacks lie split and seething, the grain gone to black.
Husks of insects crunch underfoot, thick as gravel.
crawling-stores.revelation: The store's ledger in {lair} shows grain bought and grain sold, and the grain sold was this: rotten, and sold to {town}'s bakers.
crawling-stores.rumour: bread in {town} has been making people sick

rival-delvers.situation: a hard company of delvers got here first and is stripping it

ally.notes: A hired delver the others left for dead; says they found the inner door and are breaking into {lair} now.

rival-delvers.complication: The rivals carry a writ from {town} that says the place is theirs to strip.

reward.said: what the rival delvers have already dug out

built: bedrolls, a cold fire, a map pinned to the wall
a door whose seals have been chiselled off
an inner room, its door levered off its hinges
natural: bedrolls and a cold fire on a dry ledge
a drop with new rope pegged down it
dug: bedrolls and a cold fire in a side drift
a drift cleared of fallen rock
a sealed working, its wall broken through

traces: New rope is pegged into old stone, and fresh chalk arrows point the way in.
A camp: bedrolls, a cold fire, and a map with three rooms crossed off.
rival-delvers.revelation: The delvers' map, in {lair}, was copied from an old survey that names this place and what it holds, and the survey came from {town}'s own archive.
rival-delvers.rumour: a hard-faced company came through {town} buying rope and lamp-oil and asking about {where}

bound-guardian.situation: a guardian of bone was bound to its door when the place was sealed

ally.notes: The last keeper of the place, too old to climb back up; says the guardian was bound to the door of {lair} the day it was sealed, and lets nobody past.

bound-guardian.complication: The keeper will help only if the inner room is left as it is found.

reward.said: the offering the guardian was bound to keep

built: kennel doors along a wall, bowls full of dust
a gate of bones set in mortar
a door with a chain across it, the chain worn bright
natural: a den littered with white bones
a narrowing walled with bones set in mortar
a hollow behind a chained stone

traces: Bowls are set out by the kennel doors, and they are full of dust.
White scratches criss-cross the floor, the marks of bone feet.
bound-guardian.revelation: The binding is cut over {lair}: the guardian keeps no treasure but a grave, and the keeper's own name is on it, waiting.
bound-guardian.rumour: the old keeper who lives near {where} has not come up to {town} for bread in a month

lost-party.situation: a party from the town came down a month ago, and something takes them one at a time

ally.notes: The last of a party from {town} that came down a month ago; says something takes them one at a time from the dark overhead, and it lives in {lair}.

lost-party.complication: Whoever sent the party down in {town} knew the danger, and sent them anyway.

reward.said: the party's purse, carried down to buy what they found

natural: a camp set out neatly, five bedrolls
a cave whose roof is lost in the dark
dug: a camp set out neatly in a side drift
a working whose roof is lost in the dark
built: a camp set out neatly, five bedrolls
a vaulted room whose roof is lost in the dark

traces: A camp is set out neatly, five bedrolls, and four of them have not been slept in.
Packs lie dropped where they fell, straps torn, and one boot with nothing in it.
lost-party.revelation: In {lair} the party's maps lie with the bones, and whoever hired them had already marked this place as taken.
lost-party.rumour: a party went down into {where} a month ago and only their mule came back

greedy-dead.situation: a hoard's dead owner still keeps it, and knows every coin

ally.notes: A looter of {town} who took one coin from the hoard and has not slept since; says the owner knows every coin, and sits in {lair}.

greedy-dead.complication: The looter's family in {town} spent the coin, and have been sickening since.

reward.said: the owner's grave-gold

built: coins set into the floor in patterns
carved hands reaching out of the walls, palms up
a seat of stone among heaped coin

traces: Coins are set into the floor in patterns, every one worn smooth by feet.
Carved hands reach out of the walls, palms up, as if asking for payment.
greedy-dead.revelation: The seal over {lair} says its owner was buried with all he had so that no heir could ever have it.
greedy-dead.rumour: a coin from {where} turned up in a tavern in {town}, and the drinker who spent it died the same week

last-experiment.situation: the master's last experiment broke loose, and only the apprentice is left

ally.notes: The master's last apprentice, alone since the master went into {lair} and did not come out; says the last experiment can be put down, and that it is not what the master meant.

last-experiment.complication: The apprentice wants the master's notes saved, and the notes are in {lair}.

reward.said: the master's savings, kept in a reliquary

built: jars on shelves, some with things in them that once moved
cages along one wall, opened from the inside
a workroom, a body-sized table, straps on it

traces: Glass jars stand on shelves, and some hold things that once moved.
Cages line one wall, and they were opened from the inside.
last-experiment.revelation: The master's journal ends mid-sentence in {lair}: the last experiment was the master, and it worked.
last-experiment.rumour: the old scholar who kept to {where} has not been seen in a year, and the door has not been opened
last-experiment.quest: Find what became of the master below {where}

gaol-taken.situation: the prisoners have taken the gaol, and locked the gaoler in

ally.notes: The last gaoler, locked in one of his own cells; says {leader} has the keys and holds {lair}.

gaol-taken.complication: Some of the prisoners were put here for no crime at all.

reward.said: prisoners' belongings, taken off them when they came in

built: cell doors torn off and stacked as a barricade
a walled yard open to a shaft of daylight far above
a room with a big desk and the warden's chair

traces: Cell doors are torn off and stacked as a barricade.
Pictures of the gaoler's keys are scratched on a wall in charcoal, each one labelled.
gaol-taken.revelation: The warden's book in {lair} shows half the names were sent down by one family of {town}, for debts owed to them.
gaol-taken.rumour: the old gaol was meant to be empty, but the bread cart still goes down to {where}

thing-from-below.situation: diggers broke into something older, and it came up through the hole

ally.notes: Dug too deep and broke into something older; says the thing came up through the hole in {lair}, and the rest of his crew went down it.

thing-from-below.complication: The hole goes on down, further than any rope.

reward.said: the crew's wages, dropped at the edge of the hole

dug: a drift whose floor has fallen in
a tunnel round and smooth, cut by no pick
a working that ends at a hole going straight down
natural: a cave whose floor has split
a tunnel round and smooth, cut by no pick
a cave that ends at a hole going straight down
built: a room whose floor has burst upward
a room that ends at a hole going straight down

traces: The tunnels here are smooth and round, cut by no pick.
Something has left a slick trail along the walls, high up.
thing-from-below.revelation: In {lair} the old builders had walled the hole up once already, with warnings cut in the stone; the diggers broke through the wall.
thing-from-below.rumour: the deep diggers of {town} came up early one morning, white-faced, and quit

squatters.situation: the poor of the town live below now, under a self-made lord

ally.notes: One of the poor who live below now; says {leader} takes a share of every crust and keeps the strong ones about him in {lair}.

squatters.complication: Most of the people below are not enemies, only poor, and {town} drove them down here.

reward.said: what the beggar-lord took from the poor

built: lean-tos of scrap wood along the walls
fires and pots, and somebody stirring
a raised place with a great chair on it

traces: Lean-tos of scrap wood line the walls, and a cook pot steams.
Children's chalk games cover the floor, hopscotch over the old stones.
squatters.revelation: The chair in {lair} is a magistrate's chair from {town}, and the beggar-lord sat in it once, up there.
squatters.rumour: the poor of {town} have been vanishing off the streets, and nobody looks for them

poachers-hold.situation: poachers keep their skins and their tally below, out of the lord's sight

ally.notes: A gamekeeper, caught spying on the poachers and tied up; says they keep the skins and the tally in {lair}.

poachers-hold.complication: The poachers feed half of {town} in a hungry year.

reward.said: coin from skins sold far away

natural: a cave with hooks in the roof and a stained floor
skins stretched on frames to dry
a dry cave stacked with bundled skins
built: hooks in the ceiling and a stained floor
skins stretched on frames to dry
a room stacked with bundled skins
dug: hooks driven into the props, a stained floor
skins stretched on frames to dry
a working stacked with bundled skins

traces: Skins are stretched on frames to dry, some of beasts nobody hunts near {town}.
Snares hang in bundles, waxed and ready.
poachers-hold.revelation: The tally in {lair} shows a buyer in {town} who takes every skin they bring and pays above the market for it.
poachers-hold.rumour: the game has gone from the woods above {town}, but there is always venison on the market

plague-pit.situation: the plague dead were buried here unburned, and they do not lie still

ally.notes: A healer of {town} who came down to burn the plague dead and found them walking; says the sickness began in {lair}.

plague-pit.complication: The healer has caught the sickness and will not go back to {town} with it.

reward.said: rings and coin the plague dead were buried with

built: sacks of lime heaped by the door
a ledge over a long trench
the bottom of the trench, the dead in rows
natural: sacks of lime heaped by the way in
a ledge over a long trench
the bottom of the trench, the dead in rows

traces: Lime is heaped in sacks by the door, enough for hundreds.
Bodies lie in rows wrapped in sacking, and some of the sacking is torn from inside.
plague-pit.revelation: In {lair} the first of the dead lies in a fine coat with the seal of a merchant house of {town}: the sickness came in with his cargo.
plague-pit.rumour: the plague years are spoken of in {town} only in whispers, and the pits were never marked

vault-wards.situation: an old house's wards still guard its locked fortune

ally.notes: Hired by an heir in {town} to open the vault, and left behind when the wards woke; says the heir knew about the wards, and that the true vault is {lair}.

vault-wards.complication: Two heirs in {town} both claim what is in the vault.

reward.said: the family's fortune, as it was the day it was locked

built: a vault door painted on the wall, the paint scuffed by hands
a small square vault behind a door of iron

traces: Clockwork cogs lie where something was taken apart and put back together wrong.
A false door is painted on the wall so well that the paint is scuffed by hands.
vault-wards.revelation: The family's last will lies in {lair}: it leaves everything to whoever gets this far, and names the heirs as the ones not to trust.
vault-wards.rumour: two families of {town} have gone to law over what is locked away deep in {where}

last-watch.situation: a company of the dead still holds the place for a lord long gone
last-watch.who: the dead of the last watch

ally.notes: An old soldier of {town} come to find his grandfather's company; says the company swore to hold until relieved, and its captain still holds {lair}.

last-watch.complication: The company holds for a lord whose line {town} cast out.

reward.said: pay sent at last and never delivered

built: tables and shields across the passage, manned by bones
a line of bones in rotted coats, facing the way in
a command room, a map table, a figure seated at it

traces: A barricade of tables and shields stands across the passage, still manned by bones in rotted coats.
Arrows still stand in the walls where the last attack broke.
last-watch.revelation: In {lair} the relief orders lie unopened in the captain's hand: the messenger got through, and nobody read them.
last-watch.rumour: on quiet nights folk swear they hear a watch being called, far down in {where}
